proof_summary: Write each summand as \(\binom nj\,n^{\overline j}\). Rising and falling factorials are unchanged modulo \(k\) when \(n\) is replaced by \(n+k\); using \(n^{\overline j}=j!\binom{n+j-1}{j}\) and \(j!\binom nj=n^{\underline j}\) gives termwise congruence, and the extra terms after extending the shorter sum to \(n+k\) vanish because \(\binom nj=0\) for \(j>n\).
